correctness.rationale: The Beatty complementary partition makes r(n)=K(n)−s(n), where K(n)=#{k:v(k)<n}=⌊n/φ²⌋ and s(n) counts ordered upper-plus-upper pairs. At N=v(t), K(N−1)=K(N)=t−1. Since 2<φ²<3, a representation v(j)+v(k) in {N−1,N} forces j+k=t; the irrational fractional carry separates the count A_t from t−1−A_t. Exact independent integer enumeration directly counted u+v for every t=1..250 and matched both formulas and the sum; infinite proof is the exact carry argument, not these samples.

final_claim: For lower u(h)=⌊hφ⌋ and upper v(k)=⌊kφ²⌋, the exact lower-plus-upper representation function satisfies r(v(t)−1)=A_t, r(v(t))=t−1−A_t, A_t=#{1≤j<t:{jφ²}<{tφ²}}, so the adjacent pair sums to t−1 for every t≥1.
limitations: No closed elementary formula for individual A_t; adjacent-pair result does not classify all r(n).
Earlier differently phrased Beatty identities remain a bounded originality risk.
